@dev Contract module that allows children to implement role-based access
 control mechanisms. This is a lightweight version that doesn't allow enumerating role
 members except through off-chain means by accessing the contract event logs. Some
 applications may benefit from on-chain enumerability, for those cases see
 {AccessControlEnumerable}.
 Roles are referred to by their `bytes32` identifier. These should be exposed
 in the external API and be unique. The best way to achieve this is by
 using `public constant` hash digests:
 ```solidity
 bytes32 public constant MY_ROLE = keccak256("MY_ROLE");
 ```
 Roles can be used to represent a set of permissions. To restrict access to a
 function call, use {hasRole}:
 ```solidity
 function foo() public {
     require(hasRole(MY_ROLE, msg.sender));
     ...
 }
 ```
 Roles can be granted and revoked dynamically via the {grantRole} and
 {revokeRole} functions. Each role has an associated admin role, and only
 accounts that have a role's admin role can call {grantRole} and {revokeRole}.
 By default, the admin role for all roles is `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE`, which means
 that only accounts with this role will be able to grant or revoke other
 roles. More complex role relationships can be created by using
 {_setRoleAdmin}.
 WARNING: The `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` is also its own admin: it has permission to
 grant and revoke this role. Extra precautions should be taken to secure
 accounts that have been granted it. We recommend using {AccessControlDefaultAdminRules}
 to enforce additional security measures for this role.

@title FundingVault
 @notice All-or-nothing raise for an EventYield offering.
         KYC-approved investors deposit the settlement stablecoin in exchange
         for a recorded allocation of the ATS revenue-right token. If the
         funding target is reached by the deadline, the organizer withdraws the
         raise and the platform delivers revenue-right tokens through ATS
         (which re-checks KYC on transfer). If the target is missed, every
         investor is refunded in full and the organizer receives nothing.
 @dev KYC state here is a local mirror of the ATS control list, maintained by
      the platform admin. ATS remains the source of truth and enforces
      compliance on the actual token transfer; this mirror only gates deposits
      so we never take money from an account that could not receive the token.
@notice Approve or revoke an investor in the local KYC mirror.
@notice Batch KYC update.

@notice Move the offering out of `Open`. Permissionless.
         - Funded: target reached (allowed any time), or deadline passed with
           raise >= target.
         - Failed: deadline passed with raise < target.
@notice Organizer pulls the full raise once the offering is Funded.
@notice Investor reclaims their full contribution if the offering Failed.

@notice Bookkeeping: mark that the platform has delivered an investor's
         revenue-right tokens through ATS. Does not move value here.

@title TicketEscrow
 @notice "Proof of Revenue" for EventYield.
         Every primary ticket sale routed through EventYield is paid into this
         contract in a stablecoin. The contract atomically:
           1. sends the organizer's share to the organizer, and
           2. locks the investors' share inside the contract.
         The organizer never custodies the investor share, so primary ticket
         revenue routed through EventYield cannot be under-reported.
         Resale royalties (an HTS native royalty fee whose fee-collector is set
         to this contract's address) arrive here with no function call. Anyone
         can call {syncRoyalties} to fold that surplus into the investor pool.
         After the event, an admin closes sales, snapshots the pool, and either:
           - lets ATS pay a dividend to revenue-right token holders (preferred), or
           - allocates pro-rata claims here from an off-chain balance snapshot
             (fallback), which holders then {claim}.
 @dev The stablecoin is an HTS fungible token exposed to the EVM through its
      ERC-20 facade. On Hedera the contract must associate with it once via
      {associateStablecoin} before it can hold a balance.
      Accounting invariant (outside of an un-synced royalty credit):
          stablecoin.balanceOf(this) >= poolCredited - poolDistributed
@notice Platform operator: opens/closes sales, settles, allocates payouts.

@notice The event organizer. Informational on the primary flow (their
         share is auto-transferred), used to gate organizer-only reads/actions.

@notice Associate this contract with the stablecoin HTS token (Hedera only).
         Idempotent; safe to call on networks without HIP-719 (treated as no-op).
@notice Update event terms. Locked once the first ticket is sold.
@notice Point the organizer payout at a new account. Locked after first sale.
@notice Open or close primary ticket sales.

@notice Fold any stablecoin sitting in the contract above the tracked
         owed balance into the investor pool. This is how HTS resale
         royalties (paid directly to this address by the network) are
         accounted for. Permissionless: it can only ever increase what
         investors are owed.
@notice Pull your allocated payout after settlement.
@notice Stablecoin currently owed to investors (locked in the contract).

@notice Live estimated payout per revenue-right token, pre-settlement.
 @param revenueRightSupply Total supply of the revenue-right token.
@notice Snapshot of the event's on-chain financial health for the dashboard.

@title IHRC719
 @notice Minimal interface for the Hedera token-association facade (HIP-719).
         On Hedera, a contract must be "associated" with an HTS token before it
         can receive or hold a balance of it. Calling `associate()` on the
         token's EVM address associates `msg.sender` (this contract).
         On a non-Hedera EVM (local Hardhat) this call is not available, so
         callers wrap it in a try/catch and treat failure as a no-op.

@title MockRevenueRightToken
 @notice Local-only stand-in for the ATS revenue-right security token. It
         emulates the two ATS behaviours the demo relies on:
           - a KYC / control list that gates who may receive tokens, and
           - an admin freeze that blocks a specific holder from transferring.
         On Hedera testnet this token is issued through the Asset Tokenization
         Studio UI (ERC-3643 / ERC-1400 style) and ATS enforces these rules
         natively. See docs/ATS_INTEGRATION.md.
@notice Issue tokens to a KYC-approved holder (models an ATS primary issuance).

The contract atomically:           1. sends the organizer's share to the organizer, and           2. locks the investors' share inside the contract.         The organizer never custodies the investor share, so primary ticket         revenue routed through EventYield cannot be under-reported.         Resale royalties (an HTS native royalty fee whose fee-collector is set         to this contract's address) arrive here with no function call. Anyone         can call {syncRoyalties} to fold that surplus into the investor pool.
